mainTopic: A זבה's discharge of semen, תרומה and garments touched by a כותי, and the status of צדוקי women
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing רמי בר חמא's question: does a זבה who discharges semen during her seven clean days lose her count? רבא tries to show the question cannot work, but the גמרא answers him using the זב, whose 'unbroken days' rule only blocks זיבה. So the question stands. Next, the גמרא tells how רב פפא visited רב שמואל, who served him a bull and pointed out a clash between two משניות. One משנה does not burn תרומה over the garments of a כותי, while the other burns תרומה over the uncertain garments of an עם הארץ. רב פפא's answer (a כותי חבר) is rejected. רב שימי בר אשי then explains the case as a naked כותי who went to the מקוה, which leaves only a ספק ספיקא. A new משנה discusses צדוקי women. The גמרא proves from רבי יוסי's words that for the תנא קמא, a צדוקי woman whose practice is unknown is like a כותית. Finally, a ברייתא tells of a צדוקי's spit landing on the כהן גדול. The גמרא asks why the spit was not impure simply as an עם הארץ's. אביי answers, רבא rejects his answer, and רבא's own answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The second side of the question: maybe she is only 'touching' semen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes רמי בר חמא's question. Perhaps a זבה who discharges semen is only like someone touching semen, so her count is not broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe she was only touching it, and she did not break her count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a two-sided question. Maybe the semen coming out of her counts only as 'touching' semen, which does not ruin her seven clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to see it. If the discharge is like a man 'seeing' קרי, it breaks one day of the count, as it does for a זב. If it is only like 'touching' semen, it does not break anything, since a זב who touches semen keeps his count.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. It introduces the other side of a question.
She is touching. Here it means she only has contact with the semen.
She broke or undid her count of clean days.
A woman with a זיבה discharge who must count seven clean days.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the question is whether she becomes טמאה. She is surely טמאה for the day. The question is only whether her seven-day count is broken.

phrases.english: Or perhaps she was touching
and she did not break her count?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא נוֹגַעַת הָיְתָה וְלָא סָתְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a זבה's discharge of semen treated like 'seeing' קרי, which breaks the count, or like 'touching' semen, which does not?

steps.title: רבא: she cannot lose all seven days
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the question is a mistake. Even if she did break her count, how much would she lose? All seven days cannot be right, because she should not be treated worse than the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The sharper the mind, the bigger the mistake! Even if we say she breaks her count, how much would she break? Seven days? It is enough for her to be like the man who is with her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the question itself and begins showing that no answer works. He starts with the first option: losing all seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב who has קרי loses only one day. The semen in her body came from the man, so she should not be judged more strictly than he is. Losing all seven days is therefore ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: The sharper the mind, the bigger the mistake. A remark on a brilliant scholar's error.
Even if we grant that...
Should she break or undo her count?
It is enough for her to be like the man who was with her. She is not treated more strictly than he is.

phrases.english: Rava said:
According to the sharpness is the error!
phrases.notes: He means רמי בר חמא is so sharp that his mistakes are sharp too.

phrases.english: Even granting that she breaks her count,
how much should she break?
Should she break seven?
It is enough for her to be like the one who had relations with her!
phrases.notes: A זב who has קרי loses only one day, so she should not lose more than that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the question from step 1 by showing that no answer can work.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole question. This step removes the 'seven days' option.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Breaking all seven days would make her stricter than the man himself, who loses only one day.

steps.title: רבא: she cannot lose just one day either
steps.stepSummary: Losing only one day also fails. The פסוק 'ואחר תטהר' means her seven days must come in a row with no טומאה in between. So there is no such thing as a זבה losing just one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should she lose one day? But the Torah says 'and after, she shall be pure.' 'After' means after all of them, so that no טומאה breaks up the days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his argument with the second option, losing one day. He shows that this does not fit the פסוק either, so the question has no possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אחר' teaches that a זבה becomes טהורה only after seven clean days in a row. Any טומאה in the middle forces her to start over, so losing just one day is impossible. Since seven is too many and one is impossible, רבא concludes she does not break her count at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And after, she shall be pure. The end of the זבה's counting פסוק.
After all of them, meaning after all seven days together.
טומאה that interrupts or splits the days.
The Merciful One, a name for the Torah or ה׳ as the source of the law.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's argument: seven days is too strict (דיה כבועלה), and one day clashes with 'אחר לכולן'. So the question falls apart.

phrases.english: Should she break one day?
But it says 'and after, she shall be pure'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:28

phrases.english: The Merciful One said 'after'
after all of them,
so that no impurity should separate between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes up the second option and closes off the dilemma.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'one day' option, which completes the rejection of the whole question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The seven days of a זבה must be one unbroken unit, so losing a single day is impossible.

steps.title: The same problem would apply to a זב, yet he loses one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. A זב's seven days must also be unbroken ('לטהרתו'), and yet he does lose one day for קרי. So 'one day' is possible after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to your reasoning, how does a זב himself break his count? The Torah says 'for his purification,' meaning no טומאה may split the days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reasoning. The same kind of פסוק exists for a זב, yet everyone agrees he loses just one day for קרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'no interruption' made losing one day impossible, it should do the same for a זב. But we know a זב who sees קרי loses one day. So the פסוק cannot block losing one day, רבא's argument fails, and רמי בר חמא's question stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning... It turns someone's logic back against him.
A man with a זיבה discharge who must count seven clean days.
For his purification. A word in the זב's פסוק teaching that his seven days must be unbroken.
How?

steps.whatToRemember: A זב who has קרי loses one day even though his days must be unbroken. So the 'unbroken days' idea does not rule out losing one day, and רבא's rejection is pushed back.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
how does a zav himself break his count?
The Merciful One said 'for his purification':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:13

phrases.english: so that no impurity should separate between them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reasoning from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that 'no interruption' makes losing one day impossible.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זב also has an 'unbroken days' פסוק (לטהרתו), yet he loses one day for קרי. So the same reasoning cannot block one day for a זבה.

steps.title: The same reading applies to a woman, so one day is possible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. 'Unbroken days' only means no זיבה in between, for a זב and for a זבה alike. So a זבה could lose just one day for קרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say about the זב? That the verse only means no זיבה impurity should come between his clean days. Here too, for the זבה, it only means no זיבה impurity should come between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its argument against רבא. The rule of 'unbroken days' only blocks זיבה, not קרי, for both men and women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a זבה can't lose just one day, because her days must be unbroken. The גמרא answers that a זב's days must also be unbroken, and he still loses one day for קרי. So 'unbroken' must only mean 'no זיבה in between.' The same reading works for a זבה, so רבא's rejection falls away and רמי בר חמא's question is a real question again.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity caused by a זיבה discharge
Separates or interrupts (breaks up the count)
Here too, the same is true in this case

steps.whatToRemember: The requirement that the seven clean days be unbroken only rules out זיבה. So a קרי discharge could cost just one day, for a man and maybe for a woman too. רמי בר חמא's question stands.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
phrases.notes: He means: how do you explain the זב's verse 'לטהרתו'? You are forced to read it this way.

phrases.english: That there should not be an impurity of זיבה
separating between them.
Here too,
phrases.notes: Here means the זבה and her verse 'ואחר תטהר'.

phrases.english: that there should not be an impurity of זיבה
separating between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 4 by applying the זב's reading to the זבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim (step 3) that 'ואחר תטהר' makes losing one day impossible for a זבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The זב has a matching 'unbroken' requirement and still loses one day for קרי. So the requirement only excludes זיבה, and the same must be true for the זבה.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: there is no liability for entering the מקדש because of these garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: one is not liable for entering the מקדש because of them, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the story and the question that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is talking about garments a כותי lay on. Their טומאה is only a ספק, so entering the מקדש while wearing them does not make one liable for a קרבן. The rest of the line, that we also don't burn תרומה over them, will become the focus.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering the מקדש while טמא, which normally brings liability
Liable (here, to bring a קרבן)

phrases.english: But one is not liable on account of them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the garments a כותי lay on, from the משנה.

phrases.english: for entering the מקדש, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the line: we also don't burn תרומה over them, since the טומאה is uncertain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן עַל בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the זבה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no liability for entering the מקדש, and no burning of תרומה, because of garments whose טומאה is uncertain.

steps.title: רב פפא arrives in town and hears about רב שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא comes to תואך and wants to greet a local scholar. An old woman praises רב שמואל and blesses רב פפא to be like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא came to תואך. He said: if there is a young Torah scholar here, I will go greet him. An old woman told him: there is one here, his name is רב שמואל, and he teaches משניות. May it be God's will that you be like him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that leads up to a question on our משנה. Here רב פפא learns about a local scholar named רב שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part is background. The old woman's blessing will show רב פפא what kind of person רב שמואל is.

keyTerms.meaning: A young or sharp Torah scholar
Greet him, literally 'receive his face'
Teaches or learns משניות and בריתות
May it be God's will

phrases.english: Rav Pappa happened to come to Tavakh.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: אִי אִיכָּא צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן הָכָא,
phrases.english: He said: If there is a Torah scholar here,
I will go and greet him.
A certain old woman said to him:
There is a Torah scholar here,
and Rav Shmuel is his name,
and he teaches mishnayot.
May it be God's will that you be like him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story connected to the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רב פפא is directed to רב שמואל, a respected local scholar.

steps.title: רב פפא concludes רב שמואל is God-fearing and visits him
steps.stepSummary: From the blessing, רב פפא concludes that רב שמואל is a ירא שמים. He visits him, and a bull is served in his honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: since they bless me that I should be like him, I can learn that he is God-fearing. He went to him, and a bull was prepared for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a conclusion about רב שמואל's character and goes to meet him. This sets up the Torah discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People don't use someone as the model in a blessing unless they truly admire him. So רב פפא understands that רב שמואל is not just learned but also ירא שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A God-fearing person
Learn from it, conclude from this
He set out a bull for him, meaning he slaughtered an ox in his honor

phrases.english: He said: From the fact that they bless me through him,
conclude from it that he is God-fearing.
He went to him,
he set out a bull for him,
phrases.notes: Literally 'threw him an ox.' An ox was slaughtered for a meal honoring רב פפא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: רב פפא reacts to the old woman's blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being held up as a model in a blessing shows that someone is ירא שמים.

steps.title: First side of the contradiction: no burning תרומה over a doubt
steps.stepSummary: The first משנה is quoted: we do not burn תרומה over these garments because their טומאה is uncertain. So a ספק טומאה does not lead to burning תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised two משניות against each other. We learned: one is not liable for entering the מקדש because of them, and we do not burn תרומה over them, because their טומאה is uncertain. So we see that we do not burn תרומה over a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a contradiction. It first quotes our משנה and draws a general rule from it: no burning תרומה over a ספק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה that is surely טמא must be burned. Our משנה refuses to burn it when the טומאה is only a ספק. The word אלמא turns this case into a general rule, and that rule will be tested next.

keyTerms.meaning: Set two משניות against each other, pointing out a contradiction
Burning תרומה because it became טמא
Doubt or uncertainty
Evidently, we see from here

phrases.english: He raised mishnayot against one another:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב שמואל, the host. רב פפא is the one who answers in step 11.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן ״אֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן עַל בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: We learned: 'One is not liable on account of them for entering the Temple,
and one does not burn teruma on account of them,
because their impurity is uncertain.'
Evidently, we do not burn teruma because of a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story into the Torah discussion, starting with the first source of the contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From our משנה: a ספק טומאה does not cause תרומה to be burned.

steps.title: Second side: a משנה that does burn תרומה over a doubt
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה lists six ספקות where we do burn תרומה, including a ספק about an עם הארץ's clothes. That clashes with step 9.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is a contradiction: for six kinds of doubt we burn תרומה, including the doubt of an עם הארץ's clothes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second משנה that seems to say the opposite. Here a doubt is enough to burn תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 suggested that a ספק never leads to burning תרומה. This משנה says that in six cases of doubt we do burn it, such as clothes of an עם הארץ, which his wife may have sat on while she was a נדה. Both cases involve uncertain טומאה from clothing, so why are they treated differently?

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction, setting another source against this one
The six cases of doubt where תרומה is burned
Someone not careful about טומאה and טהרה
Clothes of an עם הארץ, treated as possibly טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Both משניות deal with a doubt, so don't think one is about certain טומאה. The question is exactly why one doubt is strong enough to burn תרומה and the other is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It forces the גמרא to explain when a ספק טומאה is serious enough to destroy holy תרומה.

phrases.english: And raise a contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שִׁשָּׁה סְפֵקוֹת שׂוֹרְפִין אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: For six cases of doubt one burns the teruma,
phrases.notes: משנה טהרות 4:5.

phrases.english: for the doubtful case of the garments of an am ha'aretz!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the opposing source that contradicts the rule drawn in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule drawn from our משנה that תרומה is not burned over a ספק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משנה טהרות lists a ספק, the clothes of an עם הארץ, where תרומה is burned. So a doubt can lead to burning, which contradicts our משנה.

steps.title: רב פפא answers that the case is a careful כותי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא prays that the bull will be eaten in peace. Then he answers that our משנה is about a כותי חבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: May it be God's will that this bull be eaten in peace. What case are we dealing with here? A כותי who is a חבר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tries to settle the clash between the two משניות from steps 9 and 10. He says our משנה, which does not burn תרומה, is about a כותי who is careful with טהרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other משנה burns תרומה over an ordinary עם הארץ's clothes. רב פפא says our משנה is a different case: a כותי who is a חבר is trusted more about טהרה. So with him the doubt is weaker, and we do not burn the תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This phrase opens an answer that narrows the case.
A member of the Samaritan people, whose observance of טהרה laws was in doubt
Someone who has taken on careful observance of טהרה and מעשרות

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
May it be (God's) will that it be eaten,
this bull, in peace.
phrases.notes: This is the bull served in his honor in step 8. He is hoping his answer will be good enough so the meal is not spoiled.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With a כותי who is a חבר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to be about any כותי, which would clash with the rule about an עם הארץ's clothes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is only about a כותי who is a חבר, so his clothes are less suspect.

steps.title: רב שמואל objects that a חבר would not be called a בועל נדה
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל asks: would you call a careful כותי חבר a בועל נדה?
steps.simpleTranslation: A כותי who is a חבר, would you make him into a בועל נדה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל pushes back on רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה treats the כותים as בועלי נדה, people who have relations with a נדה. A real חבר is careful with these laws and would never be described that way. So רב פפא's case does not fit the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had relations with a נדה. He becomes טמא like her.
You make him into (literally, 'you equate him')

phrases.english: A כותי who is a חבר —
phrases.notes: The speaker here is רב שמואל, the host, even though the גמרא does not name him.

phrases.english: you make him into a בועל נדה?
phrases.notes: Our משנה treats כותים as בועלי נדה, so a careful חבר cannot be the one it is talking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּתִי חָבֵר בּוֹעֵל נִדָּה מְשַׁוֵּית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's answer that the case is a כותי חבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה calls the כותי a בועל נדה, and a חבר could never be called that, so the two do not fit together.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי gives a better answer
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא leaves and goes to רב שימי בר אשי. רב שימי says he should have answered with a different case: a כותי who went to the מקוה and then stepped on a חבר's clothes, and those clothes touched תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left him and came before רב שימי בר אשי. רב שימי said to him: Why did you not answer him that the case is a כותי who went to the מקוה and came up, then stepped on a חבר's clothes, and the חבר's clothes went and touched תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא leaves embarrassed and goes to רב שימי בר אשי. רב שימי gives him a new way to settle the clash between the two משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new case is not about a careful כותי. It is about an ordinary כותי who already went to the מקוה before he stepped on the clothes. Because he stepped on them, they become like his bedding (מדרס). Those clothes then touched the תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Why didn't you answer him?
Went into the מקוה and came up
Stepped or pressed on. This makes the item טמא as his מדרס.
The holy portion given to a כהן. It must be burned if it becomes definitely טמא.

phrases.english: He left him,
phrases.notes: רב פפא left רב שמואל, since he had no reply.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי.
phrases.english: and came before Rav Shimi bar Ashi.
He said to him: What is the reason
you did not answer him
(that it is) about a כותי who went into the מקוה and came up,
and stepped on the clothes of a חבר,
and the clothes of the חבר went
and touched תרומה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of step 11, which step 12 rejected, with a new answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a different situation (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא thought the only way out was to say the כותי himself was a careful חבר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about an ordinary כותי who already went to the מקוה, and the clothes he stepped on later touched תרומה.

steps.title: Why this case is only a doubt
steps.stepSummary: Being an עם הארץ is not the problem, because he went to the מקוה. Being a בועל נדה is only a doubt, since we do not know if he had relations recently.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you worry because of the טומאה of an עם הארץ, he already went to the מקוה. If you worry because he is a בועל נדה, it is a doubt whether he had relations recently or not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי explains why, in his case, the תרומה is not burned. Each possible source of טומאה is either gone or only a doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general טומאה of an עם הארץ goes away once he goes to the מקוה. The טומאה of a בועל נדה lasts seven days, and the מקוה does not help before then. We do not know if he had relations recently, so his טומאה is only a ספק. That is why our משנה does not burn the תרומה, while the other משנה, about an עם הארץ who did not go to the מקוה, does burn it.

keyTerms.meaning: The טומאה we assume an עם הארץ has, because he is not careful with טהרה
A doubt
Recently

steps.whatToRemember: רב שימי's answer: the כותי went to the מקוה, so the only possible טומאה left is as a בועל נדה. Whether he had relations recently is only a ספק, so we do not burn the תרומה. This settles the clash with the משנה of the six ספקות.
steps.confusionAlert: Going to the מקוה does not remove the טומאה of a בועל נדה within the seven days. That is why the doubt about whether he had relations recently still matters, even after he went to the מקוה.

phrases.english: For if it is because of the טומאה of an עם הארץ —
he has already gone to the מקוה,
and if it is because he is a בועל נדה —
maybe he had relations recently,
maybe he did not have relations recently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב שימי's answer in step 13
steps.raayaObject: That in רב שימי's case the תרומה is not burned
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: the עם הארץ טומאה is gone after the מקוה, and the בועל נדה טומאה is only a doubt

steps.title: Even recent relations only add a second doubt
steps.stepSummary: Even if the כותי did have relations recently, it is still unclear whether his wife was a נדה, so the case is a ספק ספיקא and the תרומה is not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if you say he had relations recently, there is still a doubt: maybe his wife finished counting her days from green blood, and maybe she did not. So it is a double doubt, and we do not burn תרומה because of a double doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי finishes his proof by adding a second doubt on top of the first one. This shows why the תרומה in his case is not burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first doubt was whether the כותי had relations recently. Even if he did, there is a second doubt: whether his wife counted her days from green blood and was still really a נדה. Two doubts stacked together make a ספק ספיקא, and the rule is that we do not burn תרומה for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Recently
Green, meaning a greenish blood color
A double doubt, one uncertainty stacked on another
We burn

steps.whatToRemember: A כותי who went to the מקוה creates only a ספק ספיקא, and we do not burn תרומה because of a ספק ספיקא. That is why this case fits the משנה.

phrases.english: And if you say he had relations recently,
it is a doubt whether she completed her count from the green blood,
and a doubt whether she did not complete it,
so it is a double doubt,
and on a double doubt we do not burn תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning that began in step 14 by adding the second doubt.
steps.raayaObject: רב שימי's case, in which the תרומה is not burned
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that we do not burn תרומה because of a ספק ספיקא

steps.title: But the clothes of an עם הארץ are impure anyway
steps.stepSummary: The challenge: the חבר's clothes should become impure just by touching the כותי's clothes, since clothes of an עם הארץ count as מדרס for careful people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the clothes become impure because they touched the clothes of an עם הארץ, as the Master said: clothes of an עם הארץ count as מדרס for פרושין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי is challenged about his case. Even if the כותי himself is only a doubt, his clothes should make the חבר's clothes impure for sure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי counted only two possible sources of impurity: being an עם הארץ, which the מקוה fixed, and being a בועל נדה, which is a doubt. The challenge points to a third source, the כותי's clothes, which are definitely impure for careful people. That would make the case a sure impurity, so the תרומה should be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it from a different reason
The impurity of something a זב treads or sits on, which can make people and clothes impure
People who are careful about purity

phrases.aramaic: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם בִּגְדֵי עַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: But let him derive it from the clothes of an עם הארץ,
phrases.notes: The question is put to רב שימי בר אשי, as the answer in the next line shows.

phrases.english: as the Master said:
The clothes of an עם הארץ are מדרס for פרושין!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם בִּגְדֵי עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case that steps 13 through 15 built up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי בר אשי's case of the כותי who went to the מקוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כותי's clothes are a definite source of מדרס impurity, so the חבר's clothes are surely impure and the doubt disappears.

steps.title: The כותי was naked
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי answers that the case is about a naked כותי, so his clothes never touched anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it is talking about a naked כותי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי answers the challenge by sharpening his case: the כותי was not wearing clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כותי was naked, there were no clothes of an עם הארץ to touch the חבר's clothes. Only the כותי's body touched them, and his body has only the double doubt. So the case still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Naked

phrases.english: He said to him: it is about a naked כותי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כותי was clothed, so his clothes made the חבר's clothes surely impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כותי was naked, so only the double doubt remains.

steps.title: משנה: the status of צדוקי women
steps.stepSummary: צדוקי women who follow their fathers' ways are like כותי women. Those who leave those ways for Jewish ways are like Jewish women. רבי יוסי says they are always like Jewish women until they choose their fathers' ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: Daughters of צדוקים: when they practice the ways of their fathers, they are like כותי women. If they left to follow the ways of Israel, they are like Jewish women. רבי יוסי says: they are always like Jewish women, until they leave to follow the ways of their fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It decides whether צדוקי women are treated like the כותי women of the earlier משנה or like ordinary Jewish women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא makes their status depend on how they actually behave. רבי יוסי starts from the assumption that they are like Jewish women and changes that only if they clearly follow צדוקי practice. The difference between them matters most when we do not know how a woman behaves.

keyTerms.meaning: צדוקים, a group that rejected the Sages' tradition
The ways of their fathers, meaning צדוקי practice
כותי women
Jewish women

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question in the next step: what is the status of a צדוקי woman when we do not know her practice?

phrases.english: משנה: Daughters of צדוקים,
when they are used to following the ways of their fathers,
they are like כותי women.
If they separated to follow the ways of Israel,
they are like Jewish women.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם הֵן כְּיִשְׂרְאֵלִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: they are always like Jewish women,
until they separate to follow the ways of their fathers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that builds on the previous משנה's rules for כותי women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צדוקי woman's status depends on her practice. רבי יוסי treats her as a Jewish woman unless she clearly follows צדוקי ways.

steps.title: What if we do not know her practice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the status of a צדוקי woman is when her practice is unknown.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was asked: what is the rule in an unspecified case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question that the משנה did not spell out. This sets up an attempt to answer it from the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה covers a woman who follows her fathers' ways and a woman who left them. It does not say outright what to do when we do not know which she does. Steps 23-24 answer this for the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the Sages
An unspecified case, where her practice is unknown

phrases.english: גמרא: It was asked of them:
What about an unspecified case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case the משנה of step 18 left unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of a צדוקי woman whose practice is unknown.

steps.title: The first clause suggests she is like a Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: The first clause makes women like כותי women only when they actually follow their fathers' ways. That suggests that in an unknown case they are like Jewish women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: Daughters of צדוקים, when they practice the ways of their fathers, are like כותי women. This implies that in an unspecified case they are like Jewish women!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from the first clause of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause sets a condition: they are like כותי women only when they follow their fathers' ways. That implies that without this condition, as in the unknown case, they are like Jewish women.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies, introducing an inference from the wording

phrases.english: Come hear: Daughters of צדוקים,
when they practice following the ways of their fathers,
they are like כותי women.
This implies that in an unspecified case they are like Jewish women!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 19.
steps.raayaObject: An unknown צדוקי woman is like a Jewish woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A precise reading of the first clause of the משנה.

steps.title: The last clause suggests the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The last clause makes them like Jewish women only when they left their fathers' ways. That suggests that in an unknown case they are like כותי women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the last clause: If they left to follow the ways of Israel, they are like Jewish women. This implies that in an unspecified case they are like כותי women!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by reading the last clause of the same משנה in the same precise way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last clause also sets a condition: they are like Jewish women only if they left their fathers' ways. Read precisely, this implies that the unknown case is like כותי women. The two clauses point in opposite directions, so the first proof is cancelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the last clause is right and the first clause is wrong. It is showing that each clause, read precisely, points a different way, so neither one proves anything.

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
If they separated to follow the ways of Israel,
they are like Jewish women.
This implies that in an unspecified case they are like כותי women!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cancels the proof of step 20 with an opposite inference from the same משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the first clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The last clause, read the same precise way, implies the opposite.

steps.title: Nothing can be learned from this משנה
steps.stepSummary: Since the two clauses contradict each other on this point, the משנה cannot answer the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, nothing can be learned from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that this משנה cannot settle what to do with a צדוקי woman whose practice is unknown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The precise readings of the two clauses cancel each other out, so these clauses do not decide the unknown case. The next step answers the question from רבי יוסי's line in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Nothing can be learned from it

steps.whatToRemember: When the first clause and the last clause of a משנה give opposite inferences, the גמרא concludes that the משנה cannot be used to answer the question.

phrases.english: Rather, nothing can be learned from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the opposite inferences of steps 20 and 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה does not decide the status of a צדוקי woman whose practice is unknown.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יוסי's words about the unknown case
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי יוסי says they are 'always' like Jewish women, the תנא קמא must disagree. So the תנא קמא holds that an unknown case is like כותיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוסי says they are always like Jewish women until they leave to follow their fathers' ways. This shows that the תנא קמא holds that in an unknown case they are like כותיות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof for the open question, this time from רבי יוסי's part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says the women are 'always' like Jewish women unless they choose their fathers' ways. That covers the unknown case. Since he is arguing with the תנא קמא, the תנא קמא must hold the opposite: an unknown case is like כותיות. This answers the question from step 19, which steps 20-22 could not settle.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; we learn this from what is implied
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
An unspecified or unknown case
Always, in every case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יוסי's view as the answer. The point is that his view differs from the תנא קמא's, so we learn the תנא קמא's view from the disagreement.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as we learned:
Rabbi Yosei says:
they are always like Jewish women,
until they separate to go
in the ways of their fathers.
By inference, the first tanna holds:
an unknown case is like Samaritan women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two clauses of the תנא קמא cancelled each other out, the גמרא turns to רבי יוסי's dispute to infer the תנא קמא's view.
steps.raayaObject: The status of a צדוקי woman whose practice is unknown, according to the תנא קמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה that they are 'always' like Jewish women, which implies the תנא קמא disagrees

steps.title: The גמרא accepts the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: learn from this that, for the תנא קמא, an unknown case is like כותיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question from step 19 is now answered. According to the תנא קמא, a צדוקי woman whose practice is unknown has the status of a כותית.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא קמא, a צדוקי woman of unknown practice is treated like a כותית. רבי יוסי treats her like a Jewish woman.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Affirms the inference made in step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the תנא קמא, the unknown case is like כותיות.

steps.title: A צדוקי's spit lands on the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a צדוקי whose spit landed on the כהן גדול's clothes. The כהן גדול grew worried and rushed to ask the צדוקי's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A צדוקי was talking with the כהן גדול in the market, and spit sprayed from his mouth onto the כהן גדול's clothes. The כהן גדול's face turned green, and he hurried to the צדוקי's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about צדוקים and the laws of נדה. This step sets up the wife's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול feared his clothes were now טמא. If the צדוקי's wife did not keep the laws of נדה properly, her husband's spit could make things impure. So he went to find out how she behaved.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sadducee, from a group that rejected the Rabbis' teachings
The High Priest
Spit, a spray of saliva
An incident, a story that really happened

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: There was an incident
with a certain Sadducee who was talking
with the High Priest in the marketplace,
and spit sprayed from his mouth
and fell onto the High Priest's clothes,
and the High Priest's face turned green,
and he hurried to his wife.
phrases.notes: 'His wife' means the צדוקי's wife. He went to ask her whether she keeps the laws of נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the legal status of צדוקי women to a story about how they behaved in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the כהן גדול worried whether a צדוקי's spit had made his clothes impure.

steps.title: The wife: צדוקי wives show their blood to the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The צדוקי's wife tells the כהן גדול that, although they are צדוקי wives, they fear the פרושים and show their blood to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Even though they are wives of צדוקים, they are afraid of the פרושים and show their blood to the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The wife answers the כהן גדול's worry. She tells him that צדוקי wives really do follow the חכמים in the laws of נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she shows her blood to the חכמים, she keeps the laws of נדה properly. So her husband is not considered one who is with a נדה, and his spit does not make things impure. The כהן גדול's clothes are pure.

keyTerms.meaning: The Pharisees, the group that followed the Rabbis
They show their blood to the Sages to ask whether it makes them נדה

phrases.english: She said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנְּשֵׁי צַדּוּקִים הֵן,
phrases.english: Even though they are wives of Sadducees,
they are afraid of the Pharisees,
and they show blood to the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לוֹ: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנְּשֵׁי צַדּוּקִים הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כהן גדול's unspoken question from step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the צדוקי's wife kept the laws of נדה, which decides whether her husband's spit was impure
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צדוקי wives fear the פרושים and show their blood to the חכמים, so the כהן גדול's clothes are pure.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's testimony about his neighbors
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says he knows the צדוקי women better than anyone, and they all show their blood to the חכמים. The one exception was a woman in his neighborhood who did not, and she died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: We know them better than anyone, and they show their blood to the חכמים. The only exception was one woman in our neighborhood who did not show her blood to the חכמים, and she died.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי backs up the wife's claim with his own eyewitness knowledge of צדוקי women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי confirms the wife's claim from his own experience: in practice, צדוקי wives followed the חכמים in the laws of נדה. The one woman who did not was punished with death.

keyTerms.meaning: Familiar with, well acquainted with
Neighborhood

steps.whatToRemember: According to both the wife and רבי יוסי, צדוקי women in practice showed their blood to the חכמים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּקִיאִין אָנוּ בָּהֶן יוֹתֵר מִן הַכֹּל,
phrases.english: We are more familiar with them than everyone,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the wives of the צדוקים. They lived nearby, so he knew them well.

phrases.english: and they show blood to the Sages,
except for one woman
who was in our neighborhood,
who did not show blood to the Sages, and she died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בְּקִיאִין אָנוּ בָּהֶן יוֹתֵר מִן הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יוסי's eyewitness testimony to support the wife's claim in step 26.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that, in practice, צדוקי wives did keep the laws of נדה as the חכמים taught, which is why the כהן גדול's clothes were pure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדוקי women show their blood to the חכמים. The single exception died.

steps.title: Why not worry about the spit of an עם הארץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story. The כהן גדול could have known his clothes were impure just because the spit came from an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him get it from the fact that it is the spit of an עם הארץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on the story of the צדוקי's spit. Why did the כהן גדול need to ask about the wife and נדה, when the spit was already impure for a different reason?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spit from an עם הארץ, someone not careful about purity, is impure by itself. A צדוקי would seem to fall in that group. So the clothes should be impure no matter what, and the question about נדה looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him get it (from another reason). Points to a simpler reason for the same result.
Spit, saliva
A person not careful about purity laws. His spit is treated as impure.

phrases.english: And let him derive it
phrases.notes: "Him" is the כהן גדול. He could have known his clothes were impure without asking anyone.

phrases.english: because of the spit of an עם הארץ!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the story from steps 25-26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The כהן גדול's worry about נדה in the ברייתא story
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עם הארץ's spit is impure anyway, so the clothes are impure without any question of נדה.

steps.title: אביי: the צדוקי was a חבר
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that this צדוקי was a חבר, someone careful about purity. So his spit was not impure for being an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It was a צדוקי who was a חבר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. This צדוקי kept the purity laws, so the only worry left was נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חבר is trusted with purity, so his spit does not carry the impurity of an עם הארץ. That explains why the כהן גדול only worried about the wife being a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who has taken on being careful with purity laws
A Sadducee, from a group that rejected the חכמים' teachings

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It was a Sadducee who was a חבר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the צדוקי was a חבר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any צדוקי is an עם הארץ whose spit is impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: This צדוקי was careful with purity, so only the נדה question was left.

steps.title: רבא: a man suspected with a נדה is no חבר
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's answer. The כהן גדול suspected this man of being with his wife while she was a נדה, so he can't be a trusted חבר. רבא then starts his own answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You make a צדוקי חבר into one who is with a נדה? Rather, רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי. A man you worry is with a נדה is not someone you trust with purity. Then the גמרא sets up רבא's own answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole worry in the story was that the צדוקי might be with his wife while she is a נדה. That kind of person is not trusted as a חבר. So אביי's picture doesn't fit, and רבא will explain the story another way.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who is with a woman while she is a נדה
Do you make him into, treat him as
Rather. Drops the last answer and brings a new one.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the כהן גדול knew the man was with a נדה. He means the fact that there was any worry about it shows this man was not a trusted חבר.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A Sadducee who is a חבר
you make him into one who is with a נדה?
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול worried this man might be with his wife while she was a נדה. A real חבר would never be suspected of that.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

steps.triggerLanguage: צַדּוּקִי חָבֵר בּוֹעֵל נִדָּה מְשַׁוֵּית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer from step 29 and sets up רבא's own answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's whole answer that the צדוקי was a חבר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A man suspected of being with a נדה cannot also be a trusted חבר.
